**Working paper, draft of 30 September 2026.** Wes Knipe.

[Read the PDF](files/x402_measured.pdf){.btn .btn-primary} [Read online](files/x402_measured.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

x402 lets software pay for an HTTP resource in stablecoins within the request. Raw trackers report its volume as
settled, but earlier work shows most of that is manufactured. This paper builds a weekly, reproducible, demand-cleaned
index of x402 payments on Base: settlements from 128 known facilitators, minus self-payments, closed loops,
funding-linked pairs and single-buyer dust, with every seller classified by what it sells. It reports what survives
cleaning, the split between content, data and compute, how concentrated spending is, and what a call costs, for the
weeks of late August to late September 2026.

Every number in the paper is computed from the published data at render time, and the code and data are public under
MIT and CC BY 4.0: [`paper/`](https://github.com/doescodinggiteasier/wknipe-site/tree/main/paper) in the repository.
The live, weekly-updated figures are on the [x402 Clean Index](../x402/index.qmd) page.

**Status:** draft for comment; the introduction, interpretation and conclusion are still to be written. Please cite as:
Knipe, W. (2026). *The x402 economy, measured: what AI agents actually buy.* Working paper. https://wknipe.com/paper/
